provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
The emitted program works directly on the visible grid. It reads the template from the cells of colour palette[8]. It builds the template's 8 rotation/reflection variants, deduplicated in the same order as the reference: unmirrored rotations first, then mirrored ones. It then slides every variant over the grid, staying fully in bounds, and keeps each placement whose cells are all palette[3].

The chosen placements are a maximum non-overlapping set. Ties are broken by preferring placements that need no reflection, then by the smallest solution mask over the sorted candidates, as the reference does. The chosen cells are painted palette[8].

Template matching over all orientations is unchanged by any D4 transform. Under conjugation by the episode's D4 map, the relative chirality between the template and a copy is preserved, so the reflection tie-break also keeps its meaning. For this reason no direction or axis has to be specialised from d4. Only the two colour roles become palette constants. Under the generator, all-green placements are exactly the disjoint planted copies, so the packing is unique and equals painting every match.
draft_notes.limitations: None of this has been tested; the host's verification run is the first check. If more than 40 candidate placements occur, a greedy packing is used instead of the exact one. The constructor's repair step makes that case impossible. The reference raises an assertion when tied optimal packings give different results; this program does not and returns the solution with the lowest mask instead. Demonstrations are ignored, because both colour roles are fixed by the palette. The fixtures and the stated rule appear consistent; I found no contradiction.
